C-30.Name: Large-document open on WebKit: stop O(n²) block-lexer regex scans (sticky block rules)
C-30.Summary: Opening a 4,100-line / 565 KB markdown file keeps WKWebView at 100% CPU for 23–42 s (Chromium: 1.4 s on the same build). Root cause: five `^`-anchored muya block rules (nptable, table, list, hr, blockquote) are re-run by Lexer.token() on the whole remaining document tail after every block; JavaScriptCore does not treat `^` as a hard anchor for these patterns and scans the full tail on each failed exec, so the lexer degrades to O(blocks × length). Fix: compile every non-global, non-multiline `^`-anchored block rule as a sticky regex whose exec resets lastIndex to 0 — the same match set, attempted only at position 0.

Problem.Description: Any long README, changelog, or agent log opens with a 20–40 s frozen window on macOS (the only shipping engine is WKWebView). Measured 2026-10-13: /Applications/Mark.app 2.2.0-beta, bench/big.md (500 sections, 1,501 blocks): render settles at 23.15 / 36.97 / 41.58 s. MarkView settles the same file in ~2.5 s.
Problem.RootCause: src/muya/lib/parser/marked/lexer.js runs `this.rules.X.exec(src)` per block, then `src = src.substring(...)`. In JSC (YARR), the rules whose `^` is followed by an alternation of quantified groups (hr: `^ {0,3}((?:- *){3,}|(?:_ *){3,}|(?:\* *){3,})…`, and the table/nptable/list/blockquote rules that embed it) fail slowly, proportionally to the remaining string, instead of failing at position 0. 1,501 blocks × 5 rules × ~4 ms ≈ 26 s. V8 fails these in microseconds, which is why the Playwright/Chromium e2e suite never saw it.

Evidence.Item: Renderer-only harness (vite preview + tauri-shim, unminified build of cafa8f1a): Chromium settle 1.4 s, Playwright WebKit settle 37.1 s / main-thread busy 29.8 s on big.md; rich 75-line doc 0.5 s / 1.1 s.
Layout/DOM instrumentation in WebKit: getBoundingClientRect/innerText/computed-style total less than 0.5 s; all DOM mutations land at t≈26–28 s, so the time is pure JS before the first patch.

RegExp.prototype.exec timing per source (WebKit): nptable 6.2 s, list 6.2 s, table 6.2 s, hr 3.9 s, blockquote 3.9 s, each n=1,501, called from setMarkdown → Lexer.token; total regex 27.9 s of 41.1 s. Chromium: none of the five in the top 12.
Micro-benchmark on the 565 KB string, per exec: hr as written — Chromium 0.022 ms, WebKit 6.08 ms; same pattern with the sticky flag — 0.001 ms / 0 ms.
Prototype (scratch build only, repo untouched): sticky + lastIndex-reset block rules → WebKit settle 3.5–7.7 s, main-thread busy 2.5 s (3 runs); total regex 1.5 s; Chromium and rich.md unchanged.

Goals.R-1: In blockRules.js, after normal / gfm / pedantic are built, replace every rule that is a RegExp, whose source starts with `^`, and whose flags contain none of g / m / y with an equivalent sticky RegExp whose `exec` sets lastIndex = 0 before delegating. Rules with g or m (e.g. `item` with 'gm') stay untouched. One helper, one call site; no edits to the 40 exec sites in lexer.js.
Goals.R-2: Token parity: for a corpus of fixtures (the existing markdown fixtures plus big.md-style generated input, GFM tables, nested lists, blockquotes, hr variants, front matter, footnotes, math, html), the lexer token stream is byte-identical before and after the change.
Goals.R-3: Regression gate in the engine where the bug lives: a Playwright WebKit perf spec opens a generated large document and asserts main-thread busy time stays under a budget (initially 6 s on CI hardware; tighten after a baseline), so a future rule edit cannot silently reintroduce the scan. Chromium e2e suite unchanged.
Goals.R-4: Re-measure in the real app (WKWebView via the release build) with the bench scripts used for the diagnosis; record before/after in the change completion evidence.

Constraints.Constraint: Semantics-preserving only: a `^`-anchored, non-multiline pattern can only match at index 0, which is exactly what sticky-at-0 attempts. No pattern text changes.
No new dependencies; no lexer restructuring (position-based lexing is a NonGoal).
The custom exec must also hold for String.prototype.replace/match callers of block rules (e.g. checkbox replace), since RegExpExec dispatches to an own exec.
Full vitest + Chromium e2e green; WebKit perf spec green; grace lint zero errors.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Rewriting the lexer to index-based scanning (removes the per-block substring too); revisit only if R-3 budget cannot be met.
Inline-rule tuning (entity regex ~0.5 s in WebKit) and the scattered post-render async work (settle vs busy gap); tracked as follow-ups if the R-4 real-app numbers still miss the 3 s target.
Virtualised / lazy rendering of off-screen blocks.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Unit: every converted rule is sticky, has lastIndex reset semantics (two consecutive exec calls on different strings both match at 0), and non-anchored / g / m rules are unchanged.
Unit: token parity on the fixture corpus (snapshot of Lexer.lex output before vs after).
E2E (WebKit project): large generated document opens with main-thread busy under budget; all 500 headings rendered.
Real app: bench/big.md render settles in ≤ 3 s main-thread busy on the release build; rich.md no slower than before (±10%).

AffectedAreas.M-011: muya parser block rules (src/muya/lib/parser/marked/blockRules.js) + new WebKit perf e2e spec + playwright webkit project
